newsitem.title: USA: Colonial Pipeline lifts Feb distillate allocations.
newsitem.headline: Colonial Pipeline lifts Feb distillate allocations.

text.p: Colonial Pipeline Co lifted the distillate line allocation program for February, and will not likely resume any distillate line allocations this winter, a Colonial official said.
"We took allocations off of Line 2 (Distillate Line) late Monday afternoon," said Bill Copenhaver, an operations official for Colonial at the company's Atlanta's headquarters.

He noted the company doubted any further allocations would be necessary, but that Colonial could reimpose allocations on the 888,000 barrel per day (bpd) Houston-to-New York line should the weather in the Northeast grow chilly again before the winter is over.

"If you got a real cold spell, we might start allocations again. But it just hasn't been that cold up there this winter," Copenhaver said, referring to the mild weather this winter in the Northeast, the world's biggest heat oil market.
But traders reacted to the Colonial news by pushing up NYMEX heating oil prices.

"This is bullish for heating oil just as cold weather moves into the East Coast," said a refined products trader, referring to U.S. National Weather Service 10-day forecasts starting February 16 calling for "much below to below normal" temperatures in the Northeast.

The distillate allocations began in late October of last year--and continued uninterrupted until yesterday--amid industry concern that inventories of heating oil were far too low for comfort ahead of winter in the Northeast.

But record levels of high heating oil output combined with relatively low demand brought inventories back up to more comfortable levels and set the the stage for the end of allocations, industry sources said.
Colonial Pipeline, the largest refined products pipeline in America, is a consortium jointly owned by 10 oil companies.

They include Amoco Corp, Atlantic Richfield Co, Petroleos de Venezuela SA's Citgo Petroleum Corp unit, DuPont Co's Conoco Inc, Mobil Corp, Phillips Petroleum Co, Texaco Inc, Unocal Corp's Union Oil unit, and Marathon Oil Co, a unit of USX-Marathon Group.
